title: CloverPit
genre: Roguelite deckbuilder-like / slot-machine roguelike with psychological horror (a Balatro-like, pitched as 'the demonic lovechild of Balatro and Buckshot Roulette')
release_date: 2025-09-26 (Steam, PC) [CONFIRMED – Steam/Gematsu]; Xbox Series/One + PC Game Pass day one 2025-11-20; iOS/Android 2025-12-17; PS4/PS5/Switch/Switch 2 2026-08-13 [CONFIRMED – publisher announcements via Gematsu/Game Developer]
early_access_date: n/a (free demo from 2025-04-10/11, Triple-i Initiative reveal; demo later in Steam Next Fest)
team_size: 2 people [CONFIRMED – devs: 'we're just two little Italian devs' (via PCGamesN/Game Developer)]. Likely Lorenzo Tombasi (art) and Matthew Godwarf (design/programming), the credited duo of their previous game Yellow Taxi Goes Vroom [ESTIMATE – inferred from Wikipedia credits + Xbox Wire interview naming 'Lorenzo']
developer_background: Second commercial game. The duo previously made Yellow Taxi Goes Vroom (3D collect-a-thon platformer, PC 2024-04-09, published by Those Awesome Guys), a cult hit but not a big seller. CloverPit was their first design of this type; 'getting the math right aged my brain a few years' (Lorenzo, Xbox Wire, 2025-11-20).
platforms_and_store_links: Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3314790/CloverPit/ ; Demo: https://steamcharts.com/app/3347820 ; Xbox / PC Game Pass (2025-11-20); iOS & Android (2025-12-17); PS4/PS5/Switch/Switch 2 (2026-08-13); 'Unholy Fusion' DLC and 'CloverPit: Unholy Edition' bundle: https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/72202/CloverPit_Unholy_Edition/
business_model: Premium $9.99 on Steam (frequent 10–40% discounts; e.g. $8.99 at 10% off in autumn 2025, $5.99 at 40% off in 2026) + paid 'Unholy Fusion' DLC (30 fusion charms, 11 base charms, 7 memory cards, new ending; PC ~2026-04-09, consoles 2026-08-13) + Xbox Game Pass deal + mobile version (iOS/Android) + consoles (reported at $4.99 for the Aug 2026 console launch [ESTIMATE – press snippet, unverified]).
price_usd: $9.99 (Steam list) [CONFIRMED – Steam store]; Raijin lists $6.99 at release, likely a sale/regional snapshot
units_or_downloads: 300,000 copies in 4 days [CONFIRMED – devs]; 500,000 in 8 days (~2025-10-04) [CONFIRMED – Panik Arcade via Game Developer 2025-10-06]; 750,000 in ~2 weeks (~mid-Oct 2025) [CONFIRMED – Future Friends CEO Thomas Reisenegger via GamesMarkt]; 1,000,000+ copies in under two months (~Nov 2025) [CONFIRMED – devs via PC Gamer/Game Developer]; 'a million copies across Steam and Game Pass and over five million players across PC and mobile' (Jul 2026) [CONFIRMED – console announcement press release]. Steam estimate ~1.0–1.2M units by mid-2026 [ESTIMATE – 24,160 reviews × 40–50]. Demo: 700,000+ downloads; 400,000+ wishlists pre-launch [ESTIMATE – press (Multiplayer.it), undated].
peak_concurrent_players: ~25,100–25,200 all-time peak, 2025-10-05 [ESTIMATE – SteamCharts 25,114; Raijin 25,134; Steambase 25,190 on 2025-10-05]. ~800–1,100 concurrents in 2026 [ESTIMATE – SteamCharts/Steambase/VG Insights].
steam_reviews: 24,160 reviews, ~90% positive ('Very Positive'; 21,816 positive / 2,344 negative), June 2026 [ESTIMATE – Steambase]; VG Insights 90.2% positive.
implied_review_multiplier: ~40–50 (rough): 1,000,000 copies by ~Nov 2025 [CONFIRMED] vs ~20–24k Steam reviews (24,160 in June 2026). Dates are not matched and the 1M may include Game Pass/Xbox, so treat as indicative only [ESTIMATE].
gross_revenue: Gamalytic estimated ~$6.7M gross at the 750k-copy mark (~mid-Oct 2025) [ESTIMATE – Gamalytic via GamesMarkt/WN Hub]. Steam lifetime to ~Oct 2026: ≈ $8–9M [ESTIMATE – ~1.1M units × $9.99 × 0.75 ≈ $8.2M], plus undisclosed Game Pass deal, mobile, console (Aug 2026) and DLC revenue.
net_revenue: ≈ $5.3M on Steam [ESTIMATE – $8.2M × (1 − 30%, as gross < $10M) × 0.93], before the Panik Arcade / Future Friends split (not disclosed). Game Pass/mobile/console income not disclosed.
production_cost: No disclosed figure. ≈ $100,000–$200,000 [ESTIMATE – 2 people × ~12–17 months × ~$4k–$6k/month (Italy lean indie)], plus publisher marketing (Future Friends: Triple-i showcase, trailers, PR, festival presence) not disclosed.
development_time: No confirmed figure. ~1–1.5 years [ESTIMATE – previous game shipped April 2024; CloverPit revealed with a playable demo April 2025 and launched Sept 2025]. Launch moved from 2025-09-03 to 2025-09-26 to avoid Hollow Knight: Silksong [CONFIRMED – publisher].
why_popular: A fresh twist on the post-Balatro roguelike boom: instead of poker hands you pull a slot-machine lever, stacking charms that rig the reels to pay off an escalating debt to an ATM, or fall through a trapdoor. The gambling 'one more spin' dopamine loop is tightly tuned (the team spent 'countless hours' on the sound and animation of every spin, click and jackpot). It has a creepy lo-fi first-person horror cell setting with hidden secrets, endings and lore (very streamer-friendly). It is cheap ($9.99), has a short session loop, and is easy to understand in one clip. Its 'Balatro + Buckshot Roulette' elevator pitch is instantly legible.
marketing_channels: Triple-i Initiative showcase reveal + same-day free demo (Apr 2025); Steam Next Fest; 700k+ demo downloads and 400k+ wishlists; YouTube/Twitch roguelike and horror streamers; TikTok clips of jackpot combos; publisher PR (Future Friends); release-date shift to dodge Silksong; Steam bundles with Balatro and RACCOIN; Game Pass day-one deal and fast mobile/console ports to extend the tail.
engine: no data (engine not named in any source found after 3 targeted searches)
art_style: Low-poly / lo-fi 3D first-person horror (PS1-ish grime), a single claustrophobic room with a slot machine, ATM and phone; bright 2D-ish symbols on the reels
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write the core slot/charm/modifier logic, run-state and save systems, UI and data-driven item definitions (very code-heavy, which suits Claude Code); generate low-poly room props and charm icons (Meshy/Tripo, Retro Diffusion/Midjourney), SFX for reels/coins (ElevenLabs), a dark ambient soundtrack (Suno/Udio), and flavour text and lore. | AI cannot: design and balance the probability maths and synergies (the devs said the math was the hardest part), tune the 'juice' and game feel of every spin, playtest hundreds of runs, build the mystery/lore hooks that drive streamers, or secure a publisher/showcase slot. | Toolset: Claude Code + Godot 4 or Unity + GodotSteam/Steamworks.NET; Retro Diffusion/Scenario for icons; Meshy/Tripo for low-poly props; ElevenLabs SFX; Suno music; a spreadsheet/Python Monte-Carlo sim for balance.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 3–5 weeks, $150–$400 (Claude Pro/Max $20–$200, image/3D gen $20–$60, Steam Direct $100). Excludes the developer's own living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 4–8 months, $2,000–$8,000 (subscriptions, freelance art/audio polish $1,000–$4,000, playtests, trailer, festival/marketing budget). Excludes living costs. Balancing and content variety (100+ charms) are the main time sinks.

data_conflicts: Price: Steam list price is $9.99; Raijin shows $6.99 at release (probably a sale/regional snapshot), so I used $9.99. The '1 million' figure: press framed it as 1M sales within two months, while the July 2026 console press release says 'a million copies across Steam and Game Pass', so it may include Xbox. Reveal date: 2025-04-10 (Wikipedia) vs 04-11 (Japanese press; time zones). Unholy Fusion DLC: Wikipedia lists 2026-04-09 (likely PC); the console announcement lists 2026-08-13 for console platforms. Peak CCU differs by <100 across trackers (25,114–25,190). The '5 million players across PC and mobile' (Jul 2026) mixes paid copies with mobile/Game Pass players and is not a unit figure. Engine: not found.
notes: Strong benchmark for a 2-person team: a single-room 3D scene, one core loop (pull the lever) and deep data-driven synergies produced a 1M+ seller at $9.99 within two months. The key lessons: ride a proven genre wave (Balatro-likes) with a twist that is legible in a 5-second clip; release a demo early (5+ months before launch) and stack showcases/Next Fest; avoid launching against giants (they moved from Sept 3 to Sept 26 for Silksong); then extend the tail with Game Pass, mobile, consoles and DLC. A publisher (Future Friends) handled PR, ports and showcase slots.
